requirement: Describe a Phase III, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter, 9-month study of bilateral intramuscular VM202 injections for painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

evidence.text: The protocol title and synopsis define the design and intervention.
The SAP restates the design.

requirement: Randomize in a 2:1 ratio to VM202 or placebo and stratify by baseline gabapentin and/or pregabalin use.

evidence.text: The synopsis and sample-size section give allocation and the stratification factor.
The SAP confirms separate 2:1 schedules by baseline medication use.

requirement: Define two sequential primary endpoints at Day 90: change from baseline in average 24-hour pain score and the proportion with at least a 50% reduction, both from the Daily Pain and Sleep Interference Diary.
acceptable_values: Daily Pain and Sleep Interference Diary

evidence.text: The protocol defines both endpoints and their sequential order.
The SAP confirms endpoints and derivations.

requirement: Define the two key secondary endpoints at Day 180 as pain-score change and at least 50% response, evaluated in the same sequential order after successful primary testing.

evidence.text: The protocol defines Day 180 endpoints and gatekeeping.
The SAP confirms hierarchy and reported contrasts.

requirement: Use the average of available diary scores within 14 days before each visit, require at least 5 of 7 diary days, round to one decimal, define change as visit minus baseline, and classify percent change at or below -50% as response.

evidence.text: The SAP defines diary completeness, averaging, rounding, change, and response.

requirement: Randomize at least 477 participants, 318 VM202 and 159 placebo, to retain 286 and 143 analyzable participants after 10% dropout; power both primary hypotheses at 90% using a 1.0-point mean difference with SD 3.0 and responder rates 35% versus 18%.

evidence.text: The protocol shows hypotheses, assumptions, allocation, and inflation.
The SAP repeats the calculation.

requirement: Use ITT, all randomized participants analyzed as assigned, for primary and key secondary efficacy analyses and baseline summaries.

evidence.text: The protocol defines ITT and binds it to primary efficacy.
The SAP confirms ITT use.

requirement: Define safety as randomized participants receiving at least one injection and analyze according to actual treatment, assigning anyone receiving VM202 to VM202.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the safety population and attribution.
The SAP confirms the definition.

requirement: Use mITT and prespecified per-protocol medication, dosing, and diary subsets only for sensitivity analyses, with exclusions finalized blind to treatment before unblinding.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the sensitivity populations and blinded finalization.

requirement: Analyze continuous pain change with an ITT linear mixed-effects repeated-measures model containing treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit, and baseline gabapentin/pregabalin use as fixed effects, baseline pain as covariate, unstructured within-participant covariance, and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.

evidence.text: The SAP gives the full continuous model and code skeleton.

requirement: Analyze the responder endpoint with a repeated-measures generalized linear mixed model using a logit link, the same treatment, visit, interaction, baseline-medication and baseline-pain terms, and a participant random intercept.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies the categorical repeated-measures model.

requirement: Report least-squares mean treatment differences for VM202 minus placebo at the target visit with two-sided 95% confidence intervals and p-values for continuous and responder models.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the contrast and reporting.

requirement: Control type I error through fixed sequence: test the second Day 90 endpoint only if the first succeeds at two-sided 0.05, then make formal Day 180 inferences only if both primary endpoints succeed, applying the same sequential order to the two secondary endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol defines gatekeeping across four hypotheses.
The SAP confirms the sequence and nominal level.

requirement: For missing continuous pain scores, perform sensitivity analyses using 10-fold MCMC multiple imputation and mean-of-the-other-treatment-group imputation matched on treatment, baseline medication, baseline pain, HbA1c, sex, and age, with prespecified reduction of sparse strata.

evidence.text: The SAP gives both continuous imputation strategies and sparse-strata rule.

requirement: For missing responder outcomes, derive response from imputed pain scores and also use 10-fold fully conditional logistic multiple imputation based on baseline medication, HbA1c, sex, and age; combine repeated-measures model results across imputations.

evidence.text: The SAP defines responder imputation and model pooling.

requirement: Repeat primary models on imputed datasets, observed cases in ITT, mITT, and PP populations, and datasets excluding pain observations influenced by prohibited concomitant medications.

evidence.text: The SAP enumerates population and concomitant-medication sensitivity analyses.

requirement: Summarize treatment-emergent AEs by MedDRA system organ class and preferred term, maximum severity and relationship, plus serious events, discontinuations, injection-site reactions, and prespecified events of special interest; classify missing severity conservatively as severe and missing relationship as related.

evidence.text: The protocol requires safety characterization throughout follow-up.
The SAP defines TEAE tables and missing-value conventions.

requirement: Use alternate covariance structures from compound symmetry, Toeplitz, and AR(1), choosing by lowest AIC when the unstructured model fails to converge.

evidence.text: The SAP provides the covariance fallback set and AIC rule.

requirement: Account descriptively for protocol revisions C, D, and E, including enrollment counts by revision and the changes to prohibited-medication timing and Day 270 nerve-conduction testing.

evidence.text: The SAP describes protocol-version cohorts and relevant revisions.

requirement: Ask the statistical team to approve the SAP-only MCMC, mean-other-group and logistic imputation algorithms, covariance fallback, mITT and three PP definitions, and subgroup interaction procedures before making them binding in a protocol-only plan.

evidence.text: The protocol delegates detailed methods to the SAP.
The reference SAP supplies these later operational decisions.

notes: These are confirmed-decision candidates, not facts a protocol-only model should guess.
